terms.gloss: law; in the genitive with a noun, legal: jūris scientia, legal knowledge
terms.grammar: noun, third declension; its genitive serves for “legal”
terms.comment: Latin puts the law in the genitive where English says “legal”: jūris perītus, a legal expert; jūris scientia, legal knowledge. For the law itself see law.

terms.gloss: of the law, legal (of questions and terms)
evidence: M-O s.v. legal (related to law or the legal system)
terms.comment: In this sense post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); classically “lawful” (see legal, allowed by law).

evidence: M-O s.v. legal (related to law or the legal system)
terms.comment: Quintilian’s term for the kind of question that turns on written law; post-Augustan and rare.

terms.gloss: of the courts and public business
evidence: Cic. Or. 170: ōrātiō jūdiciālis et forēnsis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of the forum, where the courts sat: what belongs to a lawyer’s work and public life.

phrases.latin: ut ēloquentium jūris perītissimus Crassus, jūris perītōrum ēloquentissimus Scaevola putārētur
phrases.english: so that Crassus was held the best lawyer among the orators, and Scaevola the best orator among the lawyers

sources: Lewis & Short: jus · Lewis & Short: legitimus · Lewis & Short: legalis · Lewis & Short: forensis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: legal (related to law or the legal system).
